name: disable-comments
notes: Adapter-authoring probe 2026-09-14: inspected the official WordPress.org Disable Comments 2.9.0 artifact (SHA-256 17bc60cc872d77f36a88fa27638bb2e15774bdd15418d966559c32cbbfe3e2c5). The range is intentionally limited to the observed release; widening it requires another artifact probe.

disable-comments.php loads the site option disable_comments_options and its settings writer persists one shared array. This capsule narrows that blob to the two endpoint toggles remove_xmlrpc_comments and remove_rest_API_comments, which the plugin consumes directly on XML-RPC and REST request paths.

The two selected values are boolean or integer endpoint switches, not entity references, credentials, counters, version markers, or page-rendered state; lint_ok records that their numeric storage must not be mistaken for local IDs. Native conformance proves each switch independently with unauthenticated request probes.

remove_everywhere, show_existing_comments, enable_exclude_by_role, disabled_post_types, extra_post_types, conditional_rules, allowed_comment_types, and blocked_comment_types remain unclaimed because they affect frontend rendering, role or post-type scope, taxonomy/template rules, or arbitrary comment types. Network settings, counters, review state, user metadata, and uninstall residue remain target-local except for the explicitly classified runtime rows.

The plugin's network option path and sitewide settings are excluded by WPrism's single-site boundary. Runtime version, blocked-attempt, review-trigger, and review-dismissal rows are named so uninstall residue remains visible without entering canonical authored state. No interpreter, provider, regenerator, or engine feature is needed.
